name: Preventable death requires strong justification
plainSummary: Frameworks that treat preventable death as unacceptable hold that when harm can be avoided through medicine, policy, or infrastructure, allowing it to occur requires a strong justification. That stance is common in public health and longevity-oriented worldviews.
whyRoot: When harm can be prevented at reasonable cost, letting it occur anyway normally requires a positive defense—otherwise neglect looks like a choice. This root ties the possibility of action to moral urgency rather than regret alone.
description: Foundational commitment that deaths avoidable through known means (medical, policy, or infrastructure) ought not to occur without strong justification; common in public-health and longevity-oriented frameworks.
